propositions: A single shared contract table drives behavioral conformance testing across lib, CLI, and MCP adapters for write operations, eliminating hand-maintained NxM parameter matrices.

The oracle asserts write-op parameter parity (force, reason, caused_by, ref, close_class) behaviorally on every adapter by executing contract cases against each transport and classifying divergences as ACCEPTED/REJECTED/PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED.
Runtime conditional rules (reason required for bug-close, close_class required) are mechanically asserted across all three adapters via dedicated contract rows that consistently reject.

MCP parameter gaps (force, reason, caused_by on transition; force on claim) are encoded as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago, keeping the suite green in CI and auto-triggering marker removal once the MCP schema is extended.
The oracle reuses the existing three-adapter harness (Outcome + Adapter protocol + Library/Cli/Mcp drivers) by extending it to thread write-op parameters, avoiding parallel test infrastructure.
A committed in-suite convergence-detection test proves the oracle detects when a strict-xfail gap (MCP parameter missing) is closed, requiring marker removal to maintain CI green status.
